Commentary.Commentary: We are back for Pakistan's reply. The two umpires and players have made their way out to the middle. It will be the left-hand right-hand combination of Saim Ayub and Mohammad Rizwan to open the innings for Pakistan. England are starting with spin in the form of Moeen Ali. Let's play...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, the game is nicely poised at the halfway mark and Pakistan will feel that they have momentum with them courtesy of their fightback with the ball. However, 184 will be far from easy on what is a two-paced surface. On the other hand, England will feel that they left 10-15 runs out there with the bat. The English pacers will look to replicate what their counterparts did on this surface and wickets in the Powerplay will be crucial. Back in a bit for the chase.

As for Pakistan, it has been a tale of two halves for them and Babar Azam will be mighty pleased with his bowlers responded in the second half of the bowling effort. They started with pace from both ends but it did not go according to the plan for them. The introduction of spin in the form of Imad Wasim resulted in a wicket but the visitors just could not build on that scalp. Imad kept things quiet from his end but the boundaries leaked from the other end. Pakistan were staring at a target in excess of 200 but reassessed their plans and realised that pace off and into the wicket was the way to go. Imad continued to hold end up but the likes of Haris Rauf and Shaheen Afridi roared back and had a big part to play in Pakistan's fightback. Except for a couple of lapses, Pakistan were pretty tidy in the field. Imad Wasim was the most economical of the lot with figures of 2 for 19 from his four overs.

A couple of lusty blows from Jofra Archer has taken England past 180 but they have fallen short, given the kind of platform that was set at the halfway mark. The first 10 overs saw England score 96 at the loss of just one wicket but the next 10 overs yielded just 87 runs, losing 6 wickets. After being inserted into bat, Jos Buttler and Phil Salt got a couple of boundaries away to get England off to a brisk start. However, Salt could not kick on but Will Jacks got going straight away. Both Jacks and Buttler capitalised on loose deliveries and kept finding the fence with regularity. However, Jacks could not convert his start into something substantial neither could Jonny Bairstow. Despite wickets falling around him, Buttler carried on his merry way and took Pakistan bowlers to all corners of the park. After Buttler fell on 84, the wickets continued to tumble during England's quest to finish on a high. Thanks to a good little cameo from the comeback man, Jofra Archer, England were able to get to 183.

An absolute beauty from Mohammad Amir to end the innings! Nails the yorker into the stumps, Liam Livingstone is baffled but manages to get his bat down and digs it out back onto the deck. England end at 183/7!

Commentary.Commentary: Digs it short and over middle, Jos Buttler skips down the track and pulls it square of the wicket where Saim Ayub does well to cut it off for just two runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.1: Mohammad Amir to Jos Buttler, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Mohammad Amir gets a change of end.

FOUR! Sliced away! After the previous over from Imad Wasim, Haris Rauf needed to back it up but instead, his over went for 17 runs. This is full and outside off, Will Jacks sees the width on offer and goes after it. Gets it off the outer half of the bat but it sails way over backward point for yet another boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.6: Haris Rauf to Will Jacks, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Sees the batter back away and follows him with a length delivery does Rauf, Jos Buttler turns it in front of square leg and gets to the other end.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.5: Haris Rauf to Jos Buttler, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Too straight again from Rauf, fuller and slower, Will Jacks flicks it off his pads to deep square leg and rotates the strike.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.4: Haris Rauf to Will Jacks, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Shot! Length delivery, slanting in, on middle and leg, Will Jacks allows the ball to come to him and whips it over mid-wicket. Shaheen Afridi gives it a chase and puts in the dive but the ball wins the race.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.3: Haris Rauf to Will Jacks, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! Stand and deliver stuff! Haris serves it right in the hitting arc, on middle and leg, Will Jacks holds his shape and does not try to overhit this one. Swings through the line and launches it over mid on for a maximum.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.2: Haris Rauf to Will Jacks, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: Begins with a low full toss, angling into the pads, Jos Buttler clips it towards mid-wicket where Iftikhar Ahmed misfields on the edge of the ring and concedes a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.1: Haris Rauf to Jos Buttler, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Haris Rauf comes into the attack.

Three dots on the trot to close out a successful over. Fractionally short and a touch slower, around off, Will Jacks rocks on the back foot in a flash and slaps it hard, only to pick out the man at cover-point. A couple of inches to the left or right and it would have been a boundary for Jacks and he knows that.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.6: Imad Wasim to Will Jacks, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Keeps it short and attacks the stumps, Will Jacks gets on the back foot and plays it with a straight bat back to the bowler.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.5: Imad Wasim to Will Jacks, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Coming in with the arm, on a nagging length, on middle and leg, punched off the back foot to mid-wicket by Jacks.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Imad Wasim to Will Jacks, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Sliding onto the pads, full in length, Jos Buttler nudges it to deep backward square leg and gets to the other end.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: Imad Wasim to Jos Buttler, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Much fuller, on middle and leg, Will Jacks firms the drive down to long on and gets off the mark with a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: Imad Wasim to Will Jacks, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Will Jacks walks out to bat at number 3 for England.

OUT! IN THE AIR AND GONE! Immediate impact from Imad Wasim! Imad starts from around the wicket and dishes out a real rank-hop, on middle. It is asking to be hit, Phil Salt rocks on the back foot and tries to muscle it towards wide long. Shaheen Afridi at long on, covers good ground to his right and slides to his right to take a well-judged catch. Phil Salt is gutted with himself as it was a hit-me delivery and he could have put it away anywhere.
Commentary.Howout: c Shaheen Afridi b Imad Wasim
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Imad Wasim to Phil Salt, OUT! c Shaheen Afridi b Imad Wasim.

Commentary.Commentary: First signs of spin as Imad Wasim is introduced into the attack.
Swing and a miss! Shaheen takes pace off and pulls his length back a touch, just outside off, Jos Buttler swings to go down town but gets undone by the lack of pace and fails to connect.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Shaheen Afridi to Jos Buttler, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! More in control this time was the English skipper. Pitched up by Shaheen, around middle and leg, Jos Buttler moves to the leg side nice and early and drills it to the left of mid on for the third boundary of the over.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Shaheen Afridi to Jos Buttler, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Lands it on a fullish length, on off, Jos Buttler jams it out towards cover where Shadab Khan collects it.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Shaheen Afridi to Jos Buttler, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Not exactly where he intended but Jos Buttler gets the result! Fuller in length, outside off, Jos Buttler backs away towards the leg side to go big on the off side. The bat turns in his hand and goes back past the bowler. Beats mid off to his right for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Shaheen Afridi to Jos Buttler, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Another yorker attempted by Shaheen that comes out as a low full toss, tailing back into the batter, Phil Salt gets his bat out in front and tucks it square on the leg side for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Shaheen Afridi to Phil Salt, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Up and over! Good-length delivery, on middle, Phil Salt holds his shape and swings through the line. He commits to the shot fully and although it comes off the inner half of the bat, the ball clears wide mid on for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Shaheen Afridi to Phil Salt, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Beats the bat yet again does Amir! End of a probing over, just 4 runs off it. Serves it on a back of a length, in the channel on off, Jos Buttler stands tall and tries to access the off side. Pokes at the delivery and gets beaten by the angle as the ball zips past the bat.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Mohammad Amir to Jos Buttler, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Digs it in short, over middle, Phil Salt swivels in his crease and goes for the pull. It comes off the bottom half of the bat but it rolls through square leg for three runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Mohammad Amir to Phil Salt, 3 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Play and a miss! Slanting away, on a hard length, outside off, Phil Salt has a loose waft at the away going delivery and gets beaten on the outside edge.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Mohammad Amir to Phil Salt, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Honing in at the stumps, on a length, Jos Buttler knocks it firmly to the right of Shaheen Afridi at mid on and calls Jos Buttler through for a quick single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Mohammad Amir to Jos Buttler, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Almost dragged it back onto the stumps! Amir misses his mark as he looks to go full. It comes out as a low full toss, outside off, Jos Buttler throws his hands at it but gets an inside edge that sneaks past the leg stump and dribbles towards short fine leg.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Mohammad Amir to Jos Buttler, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Amir lands it on a good length and gets the ball to go across the batter from over the wicket, Jos Buttler gets on top of the bounce and punches it square to cover-point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Mohammad Amir to Jos Buttler, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: It will be Mohammad Amir to share the new ball from the other end.

FOUR! Width offered and Phil Salt pounces on it! Shaheen errs in line and serves it on a length, outside off, Phil Salt goes after it as he frees his arms and flays it over cover for the first boundary of the game.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Shaheen Afridi to Phil Salt, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Well bowled! Nails the yorker, at the base of the stumps, not much movement off the air, Jos Buttler gets his bat down and digs it out to the left of mid off for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Shaheen Afridi to Jos Buttler, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Jos Buttler gets off the mark now! On a length and at pace, on the off-stump line, Jos Buttler stays rooted in his crease and extends his hands. Times the drive between cover and mid off for a couple of runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Shaheen Afridi to Jos Buttler, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Played uppishly but Phil Salt and England are away. Shaheen takes pace off cleverly and drags his length back, over middle, Phil Salt checks his shot and pushes it wide of mid-wicket for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Shaheen Afridi to Phil Salt, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Beaten! Angles it away from the right-hander, on a length, around off, Phil Salt does not move his foot much and goes for the drive away from his body. The ball nips back in ever so slightly and goes past the inside edge. It was not that far away from the off stump.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Shaheen Afridi to Phil Salt, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Shaheen steams in from over the wicket and goes full in search of swing. Ends up serving a low full toss, on off and middle, Phil Salt presents a straight bat and firms the drive to mid off.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Shaheen Afridi to Phil Salt, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for the action to start. Babar Azam leads his troops out to the middle and they are joined by the two English openers. It will be the explosive duo of Phil Salt and Jos Buttler to open the innings for the hosts. Shaheen Afridi will kickstart proceedings with the new ball for Pakistan. The countdown is done and dusted. Away we go...
Pakistan (Playing XI) - Babar Azam (C), Saim Ayub, Mohammad Rizwan, Fakhar Zaman, Shadab Khan, Azam Khan (WK), Iftikhar Ahmed, Imad Wasim, Shaheen Afridi, Haris Rauf, Mohammad Amir.
England (Playing XI) - Phil Salt, Jos Buttler (C/WK), Will Jacks, Jonny Bairstow, Harry Brook, Liam Livingstone, Moeen Ali, Chris Jordan, Jofra Archer, Adil Rashid, Reece Topley.
TOSS - Babar Azam wins the coin flip and Pakistan will BOWL first.

On the other hand, Pakistan have been in T20 mode, coming off a series win against Ireland. After a shocking defeat in the first game, Babar Azam and Co. managed to regroup and clinch the series by winning the next two matches. The Afridi duo, Shaheen and Abbas, caused most of the damage to the Irish. With no warm-up games for Pakistan before the World Cup, Naseem Shah, Haris Rauf, and Mohammad Amir seek form in this series. Mohammad Rizwan, Babar Azam, and Fakhar Zaman have stepped up at different times in the recent past and will aim for consistent performances. It's shaping up to be an exciting contest, with toss and team news on the way shortly.

England, led by Jos Buttler, are yet to play a T20I in 2024, but their players have been in the T20 groove, featuring in the Indian T20 League. The squad announcement for the hosts was headlined by the return of Jofra Archer, and all eyes will be on him as he makes his comeback. While Phil Salt and Will Jacks had impactful performances, the performances of Moeen Ali, Sam Curran, Jonny Bairstow, and Liam Livingstone for their respective Indian T20 League franchises left a lot to be desired, and they will be eager to get back to their best ahead of the World Cup.

Hello and a warm welcome, folks, to our coverage of the 2nd T20I between England and Pakistan at Edgbaston in Birmingham. After the series opener was washed out, both teams will be eager to make the most of the remaining three matches, with the T20 World Cup just around the corner. The weather looks much more promising, and although clouds are hovering, let's hope for an uninterrupted game.
... MATCH DAY ...

The ICC T20 World Cup 2024 is fast approaching, and teams are in their final preparation stages. England, genuine title contenders, face a formidable Pakistan side in a four-match T20I series. The first game was washed out due to rain, disappointing Pakistan as they were counting on this match for final evaluations before announcing the World Cup squad. England boasts an impressive lineup, with Phil Salt and captain Jos Buttler showcasing their skills in the Indian T20 League before rejoining the national side. Their middle order is stacked with power-hitters like Will Jacks, Liam Livingstone, and Moeen Ali. A significant boost for England is the return of Jofra Archer, who has been in fiery form in domestic games. Speedsters Mark Wood and Reece Topley add further strength to their bowling attack. Adil Rashid, their main spinner, has performed well in this format recently, with Ali offering solid support. Pakistan, meanwhile, has shown inconsistency in recent series. The reappointment of Babar Azam as captain could be pivotal, but it remains to be seen if he can deliver the desired results. The bulk of the scoring responsibility will fall on the skipper, along with Mohammad Rizwan, Saim Ayub, and Fakhar Zaman, who have all been in good form. Azam Khan and Iftikhar Ahmed are expected to provide late-order firepower, while spinning all-rounders Imad Wasim and Shadab Khan are crucial for their dual contributions. Their pace attack, featuring Naseem Shah, Haris Rauf, and Shaheen Afridi, is one to watch. They have the potential to dismantle any batting lineup if they perform to their capabilities. Both teams are eager for victory, Pakistan ​​​​​​ to boost morale and England to carry winning momentum into the World Cup. The Men in Green will need to address their recent inconsistencies and focus on cohesive team performance. Their strategy will likely revolve around leveraging their potent pace attack and ensuring their top order provides a strong foundation. On the other hand, England's strategy will hinge on their explosive batting lineup and the experience of their seasoned bowlers to keep the pressure on the visitors. In conclusion, this series promises intense competition, with both sides aiming to fine-tune their strategies and secure a psychological edge ahead of the World Cup. Fans eagerly await to see which team will emerge victorious in this critical preparatory phase.
